newsitem.title: USA: ITT executives will not tender shares.
newsitem.headline: ITT executives will not tender shares.

text.p: Top executives of ITT Corp vowed Wednesday to retain their ITT shares as an expression of confidence in the company's restructuring plan.
Prodded by an investor during a conference call, Chairman Rand Araskog said he did not intend to tender his shares in a $2.1 billion stock buyback announced by the company earlier today.
When first questioned about his plans, Araskog said the status of his holdings was a private matter.
"It would be a strong vote of confidence in the stock if you were to say now that you do not plan on tendering," said the investor.
"Then you've got a strong vote of confidence in the stock," Araskog responded.
Other top executives participating in the call also said they would not tender their shares.
ITT, fighting a takeover bid by Hilton Hotels Corp, today announced plans to split the company in three, repurchase 30 million shares at $70 each, and buy back $2.0 billion of debt.
